name: Lay mines
summary: A unit plants mines that the enemy can't easily see or target and that wait for contact. The first enemy to drive or walk over one, or to come very close, sets it off: an anti-tank mine wrecks or cripples a vehicle, an anti-personnel mine hurts every soldier near the blast, and a snare holds its victim instead. Friendly units pass safely or are steered around them. The owner sees its own mines, works from a small stock that only a resupply point or time refills, and is often far away when one goes off. The counterplay is information: detectors, sweepers and scans reveal mines, which can then be defused or set off from a safe distance, and fliers never touch them. The levers are what triggers a mine, what it does, how many can be out at once and how a hidden mine can be found.
counterplay: Bring detection: a detector, a scan or a scout's mark reveals mines to the whole team, and a revealed mine can be driven around.
Sweep them: engineers with a sweeper kit or a repair tool defuse revealed mines in seconds, so cover them while they work.
Set them off from a distance: splash, shelling or fire aimed at suspect ground clears a minefield (Red Alert 1 Yaks strafe mined ground; Company of Heroes mortars shell it).
Fly over them: ground mines never touch aircraft, and fliers can also hunt a planter that has to stop to lay them.
Send the wrong target first: soldiers cross anti-tank mines safely and vehicles shrug off anti-personnel ones, so let the unit the mine ignores lead or clear the route.
Leave the obvious paths: mines sit on roads, chokes, doors and ore fields, so take the long way or follow a teammate's tracks.
Use mine-proof kit where the game has it, such as PlanetSide 2's Mine Guard or Company of Heroes' flail tanks, to survive a blast or plough straight through.

other_examples.unit: Mines (every faction) and Panzer Elite Teller Mines, with the Company of Heroes 2 TM-35
other_examples.note: Engineers, some infantry and a few light vehicles spend munitions to plant mines in sets of three. Once built they turn invisible to the enemy, friendly units cross them freely, and contact with any enemy sets off a wide blast that usually kills the soldier who trips it, badly hurts the rest of his squad and is almost sure to wreck a vehicle's engine or tracks; the blast hurts friends nearby too. Engineers with a minesweeper upgrade spot mines from a distance and defuse them on their own, detected mines can be shot or shelled, and flail or plough tanks drive straight through. The Teller variant ignores infantry and saves its charge for vehicles. In the sequel the Soviet engineers' TM-35 goes off under any enemy, and their sweeper kit takes the place of one of the squad's rifles.

sources.title: Mines, Company of Heroes Wiki
sources.version: Company of Heroes with Opposing Fronts and Tales of Valor

sources.title: Teller Mines, Company of Heroes Wiki
Combat Engineers, Company of Heroes Wiki

other_examples.unit: Demo Trap (GLA), built by the Worker
other_examples.note: The GLA Worker builds explosive traps one at a time, usually at chokes and base entrances. A finished trap turns stealthy, and its owner sets it either to go off when an enemy comes near or to wait for a manual order; stealthed units still trigger it. One blast can destroy a main battle tank. Stealth-detecting units reveal a trap, after which almost anything can destroy it from outside its blast, and in Zero Hour Workers can defuse traps, at the risk that the owner blows one as they approach.

An upgrade bought per building rings a Chinese structure with mines that its owner sees as blinking lights and the enemy does not see at all; spent mines grow back slowly while the building stands. The Cluster Mines general's power has a cargo plane scatter a minefield anywhere, and those do not grow back. Mines go off when an enemy comes close or when explosive splash or fire reaches them, but bullets leave them alone. Detection reveals them, and Dozers and Workers disarm the ones they can see.

A researched upgrade gives each Vulture three mines, which never come back once used. A mine burrows where it is laid and takes no orders; when a ground enemy enters its sensor range it digs out, runs to the target and explodes. Fliers and hovering ground units such as workers and Vultures pass over them unharmed. Mines go after cloaked ground units without needing a detector but do not reveal them, and ranged units can shoot mines they can see before reaching them.

sources.title: Template:SC1SpiderMine (the StarCraft ability box shown on the Spider mine page), StarCraft Wiki

other_examples.note: A small robot that is itself the mine: it walks into place and burrows, and only then can it attack, firing one missile with a wide splash at an enemy that comes near and then reloading. It is cloaked while burrowed but shows itself while it reloads, a change a 2017 patch made so that mines left alone are easier to clean up, and a later patch warns players when one burrows within range of their units. In development it was a suicide unit that clung to a target and blew up after a delay.

other_examples.unit: Mine Drop and Magnetic Mine Drop (Nod support powers)
other_examples.note: A bomber scatters a wide field of nearly invisible mines; it can be shot down before it releases them, and stealth-detecting units such as the GDI Pitbull destroy the mines from a safe distance. In Kane's Wrath the Marked of Kane version drops mines that cling to the first vehicle over them and eat away its hull over time; they ignore infantry and only repair drones can remove them, so they behave like an infester left lying on the ground.

sources.title: Magnetic mine drop, Command & Conquer Wiki

other_examples.note: Places a row of cloaked mines on the battlefield. Once they arm, contact sets one off and its blast chills or freezes the enemies around it rather than only hurting them; air units take no damage. A mine whose payload is a freeze, which feeds the same leader's shatter powers.

shooter_analogues.note: Engineers lay anti-tank mines that go off when an enemy vehicle passes close, and one blast leaves even heavy armour unable to move. Friendly mines are highlighted for the team, while enemy mines stay unmarked until someone spots them; thermal optics show them clearly. Any weapon can destroy a mine, and an Engineer can pick it up or disarm it with the repair tool or the remote bomb-disposal bot. Mines outlast the death of the player who laid them, laying one past the cap removes the oldest, ammo boxes refill them, stacked mines blow as one big charge, and friendly vehicles never set them off.

sources.title: M15 AT Mine (Anti-Tank Mine/Battlefield 4), Battlefield Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: An Engineer carries a few anti-vehicle mines that explode when an enemy vehicle, or a soldier in a MAX suit, moves close; soldiers on foot don't set them off but are still hurt by the blast. Mines stack, stay after the owner dies or changes class, and can be shot, or defused with the repair tool's alternate fire for experience. Players lay them on supply routes, on vehicle spawn pads and under parked spawn vehicles. Vehicles answer with Mine Guard, a defence slot that cuts the damage they take from mines.

The advanced engineers plant proximity charges that blow up when an enemy player comes near, and teams use them to guard building entrances and chokes against infiltrators. Each team shares one limit, and planting past it removes that team's oldest charge.

sources.title: Feather proximity C4, Command & Conquer Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: A thrown trap that snaps shut on the first enemy who comes too close, damaging them and holding them in place for a moment. It arms after a short delay, only one can be out at a time, and enemies can destroy it before it springs. Junkrat sees his trap through walls and gets a cue when it catches someone or is destroyed, so it doubles as a flank alarm; a few movement and protective abilities free the victim or keep the trap from closing.

player_translation.summary: A light planter (an engineer, a minelayer truck or a utility drone) carries a small stock of mines, plants them where enemies have to pass and gets a ping when one goes off. Mines stay hidden from enemies until revealed, arm after a short delay, never trigger for friends, and cripple or wound rather than erase, so the victim keeps a reaction and the enemy team gets a job: detect, sweep or blow them up.
as_user: You buy a fast, lightly armed or unarmed unit and carry a few mines, shown as pips. Press Q to plant one where you stand; a vehicle drops it under its rear. Planting takes a moment, and you are exposed while you work.

The skill is reading the map: where vehicles must drive, which door the flankers use, which route the harvesters and supply runs take. Pair mines with wire or walls that funnel enemies into them, and with a teammate's guns covering the field.

You see your own mines through walls and on the minimap. When one triggers you get a ping, the kill credit and a glimpse of who set it off, even from across the map, so a minefield is also a tripwire.

Your stock refills at a resupply point or from a teammate's supply kit, not on its own (the snare variant recharges on a cooldown instead). Only a few mines can be out at once; planting past the cap removes your oldest.
Your variant or your team's flavour decides the mine: anti-tank mines ignore soldiers and cripple vehicles, anti-personnel mines hurt the soldiers near the blast and barely scratch vehicles.
as_target: You can't see an enemy mine until someone reveals it: a detector, a scan, a scout's mark, or coming very close, where it shows a faint glint just ahead of you. A revealed mine is marked for your whole team.

If you set one off, the blast is loud, clear and names the planter. A vehicle loses its tracks or engine for a while and takes heavy damage, but a full-health vehicle survives; a soldier is badly hurt rather than killed outright.
Right now you can stop and scan, fire at suspect ground, call an engineer to sweep it with the repair tool, take another route, or let the unit type the mine ignores go first.
A crippled vehicle in a minefield is bait: expect the planter's team to follow up, and get your crew out or your support in.
teammates: The planter's team guards the minefield with guns, funnels enemies with cover or wire, and pings the routes the enemy uses; resupply players refill the planter's stock.
The enemy team sweeps with repair tools, reveals with scouts and detectors, clears suspect ground with aircraft and artillery, and sends infantry ahead to check the road for its vehicles.
A crippled vehicle sets up a kill: anti-armour teammates finish what the mine stopped, as Company of Heroes players pair minefields with gun emplacements.
Bait and trap: a planter retreats through a mined doorway so its chasers run into the mine.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse fires the unit's weapon, if it has one.

Q: tap to plant a mine at your feet (a vehicle drops it under its rear). While you carry mines, a ring at your feet always shows the trigger radius the next one will have. The mine arms after a short delay, shown as a filling ring.
Your mines show as team-coloured icons through walls, and middle mouse (the universal ping) on one marks it for your teammates.

The pattern spends one counted key (Q), within the T1 budget. On a command-trigger card, holding Q for a moment sets off all your mines at once, while a tap still plants; the snare and mine-drop variants use the same key.
Victims and sweepers use the tools they already have: the repair tool's main fire on a revealed mine defuses it, and any weapon can shoot it.
feedback: Planting: a short hatch or digging animation and sound, then an arming ring, and a soft beep when it arms that only the planter's team hears.
Own mines: team-coloured icons on the ground and the minimap. Enemy mines: nothing until revealed, then a red icon for the team that revealed them.
Close range: a faint glint on the ground a few steps ahead, so a careful player can spot a mine without a detector.
Trigger: a sharp click, then a big, readable blast with a shockwave mark on the ground, a mine icon and the planter's name in the kill feed, and a ping on the planter's minimap.
A crippled vehicle shows broken tracks and smoke, and its crew gets a 'tracks damaged' banner with a repair timer.
changes_from_rts: Red Alert 1 mines can't be selected or targeted and stay until something sets them off; only fire aimed at the ground clears them. A player needs agency, so here mines can be revealed by detectors, scans and a close-range glint, swept with repair tools and set off from a distance.

In Red Alert 1 one mine kills most vehicles and one blast can wipe out a squad. Against people, anti-tank mines cripple and badly hurt rather than kill a full-health vehicle, and anti-personnel mines wound, so a hidden trap is a setback, not a lottery death.
Red Alert 1 decides the mine by side (anti-tank for the Allies, anti-personnel for the Soviets); here it is a variant or a flavour lean, and the card must say which so enemies can read it.
An arming delay and a cap per player (and per team, as in Renegade) stop mine spam and stop a mine being dropped under a chasing enemy as an instant weapon.
The Red Alert 1 minelayer refills its five mines for free at a depot; here the stock refills at resupply points or from teammates, which gives support players a job.
Mines stay after the planter dies (as in Battlefield 4 and PlanetSide 2) but vanish when the player switches unit or after a long time, so the map doesn't fill up with stale traps.
From a top-down camera a mine is a few pixels, so icons, the glint and loud, clear blasts must carry what the RTS showed through selection and unit lists.

team_play.notes: Mines create jobs on both sides: the planter, the guns that cover a minefield and the resupply that refills it, against scouts with detectors, sweeping engineers and drivers who wait for a cleared road. Every trigger also tells the planter's team where the enemy is.

notes: Placing an object with a trigger radius and an arming delay is simple.

Visibility per team is the hard part: a mine must be hidden from one team and shown to the other, with reveal rules for detectors, scans and close range, all decided by the server so no client knows where hidden mines are.
Caps per player and per team, persistence after death, ownership for kill credit, friendly fire and stacking all need clear rules.
Interactions: splash and fire that set mines off, repair tools that defuse them, flying units that ignore them, and vehicle crippling (track or engine damage) as a state of its own.
UI: the owner's icons, reveal markers, the glint, the trigger ping and the kill-feed entry.
Hidden kills feel unfair; keep a blast below a full-health kill or make detection easy.
Mine spam at a choke, a spawn or a vehicle pad (a common PlanetSide 2 tactic) can lock a route; cap mines per player and per team and keep spawn areas clear of them.
Stacking mines into one huge blast (Battlefield 4, PlanetSide 2) turns a cheap planter into a tank killer; stacked mines should not add up past a limit.
A mine that never triggers is wasted effort, and a mine that is too weak is never planted; the payoff has to be worth the planter's time away from the fight.
A tiny hidden object is hard to read from above; the glint, reveal icons and a loud trigger have to carry it.
Once a mine is revealed, players must tell an anti-tank mine from an anti-personnel one, and their own team's mines from the enemy's.
After a trigger, who planted the mine and where the minefield lies must be clear, or deaths feel random.

variants.name: Anti-tank mine
variants.summary: Only vehicles and walkers set it off; soldiers cross it safely. It does heavy damage and cripples tracks or engine.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 Allied minelayer, Company of Heroes Teller Mines, Battlefield 4 M15 AT Mine, PlanetSide 2 Tank Mines

counters.why: Wrecks or cripples the ground vehicles that drive over it, leaving them stuck for teammates to finish.

countered_by.why: Soldiers walk over anti-tank mines without setting them off and can clear the route for their own vehicles.
Fliers never touch ground mines and can hunt a planter that has to stop to lay them.
A detector shows hidden mines to its team, which can then drive around them or shoot them from a safe distance.
A repair tool defuses a revealed mine in seconds, so engineers clear a path for their team.
Splash and shelling set mines off from a distance, so a suspected minefield can be cleared before anyone walks in.

variants.name: Anti-personnel mine
variants.summary: Soldiers and small drones set it off; the blast hurts every soldier near it but barely scratches vehicles, which can roll straight over it.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 Soviet minelayer, Renegade proximity C4

counters.why: Hurts every soldier caught near the blast, so it punishes groups and flankers on foot.

countered_by.why: Vehicles shrug off anti-personnel mines and can drive through a field to clear a path.
Fliers never touch ground mines and can hunt a planter that has to stop to lay them.
A detector shows hidden mines to its team, whose soldiers can then step around them or shoot them from a safe distance.
A repair tool defuses a revealed mine in seconds, so engineers clear a path for their team.
Splash and shelling set mines off from a distance, so a suspected minefield can be cleared before anyone walks in.

variants.name: Snare trap
variants.summary: Holds instead of blowing up: the first enemy to touch it is rooted (or slowed, or frozen with a cold payload) for a moment and takes light damage, and the owner gets a ping. One or two at a time, recharging on a cooldown; enemies can shoot an unsprung trap.
variants.seen_in: Overwatch Junkrat's Steel Trap; Halo Wars 2 Cryogenic Generator (a freezing payload)

adds_strengths.why: The first enemy over the trap is held in place for a moment and you get a ping, so you or a teammate can finish it.

adds_weaknesses.why: A snare does little damage by itself and only one or two can be out at once, so it needs a follow-up to pay off.

variants.name: Command trigger
variants.summary: Each mine can be set to go off by itself or only on your order, so it can wait for the best target (the tank, not the scout in front of it). Enemies who reveal it can defuse it, but the owner can blow it as they work.
variants.seen_in: Generals Demo Trap (proximity fuse or manual control); the StarCraft: Ghost demo's spider mines

variants.name: Seeker mine
variants.summary: A buried mine senses a nearby enemy, digs out and scuttles to it before exploding, so a near miss still counts; it can be shot while it runs.

variants.name: Mine drop
variants.summary: A flier scatters a spread of hidden mines along its flight path or onto a marked spot, and is exposed to anti-air while it flies the run.
variants.seen_in: Generals Cluster Mines, Company of Heroes Butterfly Bombs, Tiberium Wars Mine Drop, Halo Wars 2 Cryogenic Generator

variants.name: Mine belt
variants.summary: While the unit stands still it seeds a few hidden mines around itself that grow back slowly; when it moves on, they lapse after a short time.
variants.seen_in: Generals Chinese Land Mines (a building upgrade whose mines grow back)

variants.name: Be the mine
variants.summary: The unit burrows or hunkers down to become a hidden mine itself: it fires one heavy blast at the next enemy that comes in range, shows itself while it reloads, and must unburrow before it can move.

adds_strengths.why: Hidden while it waits, it lands one heavy splash shot on the next enemy that comes near, then reloads.

adds_weaknesses.why: Can't move while it waits and shows itself while it reloads, so a detector or anyone who saw it fire can kill it.

countered_by.why: A detector reveals it while it waits, and it must unburrow before it can move, so it can be shot from outside its short reach.
Once it is revealed, or while it shows itself reloading after a shot, long-range guns kill it from outside its reach.

adds_strengths.why: Its hidden mines keep hurting or stopping enemies on routes it is no longer watching, and every trigger pings it.

adds_weaknesses.why: A mine does nothing until an enemy touches it, the stock is small, and detection, sweeping or a blast at the ground removes it.

counters.why: Mines at doors and side paths catch saboteurs and sneaking flankers, cloaked ones included.
Harvesters and supply runs follow set routes, so a mined route or resource field catches them.

countered_by.why: Fliers never touch ground mines and can hunt a planter that has to stop to lay them.
A detector shows hidden mines to its team, which can then drive around them or shoot them from a safe distance.
A repair tool defuses a revealed mine in seconds, so engineers clear a path for their team.
Splash and shelling set mines off from a distance, so a suspected minefield can be cleared before anyone walks in.

open_questions: Should enemy mines be fully invisible until revealed, or show a faint glint at very short range as proposed here?
Do mines stay after their planter dies (Battlefield 4, PlanetSide 2), and for how long?
One cap per player, one per team (Renegade), or both?
Should an anti-personnel mine ever kill a full-health soldier, and may a blast hurt the planter's own team (Company of Heroes) or only enemies?

shooter_fit.reason: A staple of team shooters (Battlefield, PlanetSide 2, Renegade, Overwatch's traps) that gives engineers and defenders a job and the enemy a counter-pick, but hidden traps need caps, detection and loud tells to read well from above.
